title: Tor-independent derived base change for qcqs algebraic-space morphisms
statement:
Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme]. Work with algebraic spaces over $S$, their small etale structure sheaves [def-trf-algebraic-space], and the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Use module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], their unbounded derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], and quasi-coherence [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module]; $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}$ is the full subcategory with quasi-coherent cohomology. Use the canonical module tensor pullback and direct image [def-trf-space-etale-module-functors], with their derived functors and composition comparisons [lem-sfb-space-derived-etale-chart-calculus], computed by flat-term K-flat and K-injective resolutions. Let $f:X\to Y$ and $g:Y^\prime\to Y$ be morphisms of algebraic spaces, and put $X^\prime=X\times_Y Y^\prime$, with projections $g^\prime:X^\prime\to X$ and $f^\prime:X^\prime\to Y^\prime$ [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. Assume $f$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated: on etale scheme charts its inverse images of quasi-compact opens are quasi-compact and its relative diagonal is quasi-compact. Assume $X$ and $Y^\prime$ are Tor independent over $Y$, meaning that for every pair of geometric points $\bar x:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to X$, $\bar y^\prime:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to Y^\prime$ with common composite $\bar y$ and $\Omega$ algebraically closed, $\operatorname{Tor}^{\mathcal O_{Y,\bar y}}_n(\mathcal O_{X,\bar x},\mathcal O_{Y^\prime,\bar y^\prime})=0$ for all $n>0$ [def-weil-pbc-tor-modules]. For every $E\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X)$ the canonical derived base-change morphism is an isomorphism in $D(\mathcal O_{Y^\prime})$:
$$\beta_E:Lg^*Rf_*E\xrightarrow{\sim}Rf^\prime_*L(g^\prime)^*E.$$
Precisely, $\beta_E$ is adjoint under $L(f^\prime)^*\dashv Rf^\prime_*$ to $L(f^\prime)^*Lg^*Rf_*E\simeq L(g^\prime)^*Lf^*Rf_*E\to L(g^\prime)^*E$, with the last arrow induced by the counit of $Lf^*\dashv Rf_*$. No flatness of $f$ or $g$, boundedness of $E$, properness, finite presentation or Noetherian hypothesis is required.

source.place: Tag 08IR, lemma-compare-base-change, full statement and canonical comparison in the first sentence of its proof.

proof.text: Isomorphisms of derived module objects can be checked after jointly surjective etale restriction: restriction is exact by the chart-calculus statement, so commutes with each cohomology; local inverses of cohomology sheaf maps glue uniquely, and the derived cohomology criterion then detects an isomorphism. Choose affine etale charts $V\to Y$ and affine etale charts $V'\to Y'\times_YV$. These cover $Y'$ by the atlas and fibre-product statements. The chart calculus identifies both restrictions of the exchange square with the square over $V'\to V$; its comparisons preserve the adjunctions, and mate pasting identifies the restricted arrow with the counit-defined $\beta$ for that square. The geometric-local-ring chart identifications preserve Tor independence: on any further etale scheme chart the three rings in its definition are unchanged. It therefore suffices to treat $Y=\operatorname{Spec}R$ and $Y'=\operatorname{Spec}C$. The base morphism $g$ is now affine and $h=g'$ is affine by affine permanence.

source.place: Tag 08IR, proof, first reduction to affine schemes.

proof.text: The reduced morphism $f$ and its base change $f'$ are qcqs. Quasi-compactness is stable under base change by the affine-test theorem; the diagonal of the changed morphism is the base change of the original diagonal, so that same quasi-compactness assertion preserves quasi-separatedness. Apply the derived-pushforward theorem to $f$ and $f'$: it requires only relative qcqs, not absolute qcqs of the spaces. Apply the derived-pullback/tensor theorem to $g$ and $h$. Consequently both the source and target of $\beta_E$ have quasi-coherent cohomology. Affine derived conservativity for $g$ reduces the assertion to invertibility of $Rg_*\beta_E$.

Put $\mathcal A=g_*\mathcal O_{Y'}$ and $\mathcal B=h_*\mathcal O_{X'}$. The normalized affine pull-push statement makes $\mathcal A$ quasi-coherent, and ordinary affine module base change gives $f^*\mathcal A\cong\mathcal B$. The affine associated-module equivalence identifies $\mathcal A$ with $a_R(C)$: its sections on $\operatorname{Spec}R$ are $C$ by the direct-image definition. We prove that the resulting augmentation $c:Lf^*\mathcal A[0]\to\mathcal B[0]$ is invertible. Choose any affine etale chart $U=\operatorname{Spec}A\to X$. By chart calculus the restriction is the augmentation for $U\to\operatorname{Spec}R$, with coefficient the associated module of $C$. The canonical Zariski-etale equivalence and the affine derived-pullback computation identify this arrow with the associated sheaf of $A\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}C\to(A\otimes_RC)[0]$. These are the canonical comparisons: on a common K-flat representative the coefficient map is the resolution augmentation tensored with $A$, and the normalized word-comparison theorem descends that same map. The existing etale-chart criterion turns geometric Tor independence into the ordinary local-ring condition on scheme atlases. Restricting the atlas to $U$ gives that condition for $A,C$ over $R$; the ring local criterion then makes the displayed augmentation an isomorphism. Exact etale restrictions and the cohomology criterion, as in step 1, imply that $c$ is invertible on $X$.

proof.text:
Use the normalized affine exchange identity with this $f,g,E$. Its hypotheses hold by step 2, in particular $Rf_*E$ has quasi-coherent cohomology. In its notation the equation is
$$Rg_*(\beta_E)\lambda_{g,Rf_*E}=Rf_*(\lambda_{h,E})\,Rf_*(1_E\otimes^{\mathbf L}c)\,\pi_{f,E,\mathcal A}.$$
The projection formula applies to $f$, $E$ and $\mathcal A[0]$: $f$ is qcqs, $E$ has quasi-coherent cohomology by hypothesis, and $\mathcal A$ is quasi-coherent by step 3. Thus $\pi_{f,E,\mathcal A}$ is an isomorphism. Both $\lambda$ maps are isomorphisms by the affine exchange input, while $c$ is an isomorphism by step 3. Tensor and direct-image functors take an inverse to an inverse, so every factor on the right is invertible; the displayed equation proves $Rg_*\beta_E$ invertible. Affine conservativity from step 2 gives $\beta_E$ invertible, and the restriction argument of step 1 gives the original assertion. The equation fixes the actual adjunction-mate map throughout, rather than merely an isomorphism of its two objects.

Every hypothesis holds and proof_deps equal the union of the step uses.
